patients.summary: Healthy 44-year-old corporate sales manager who joined in late 2023 with no problems or medications. Right Bell palsy in June 2025 treated at ENT with steroids, fully recovered by his October 2025 physical; a same-side recurrence in February 2026 was handled in the ED after his last practice visit.

documents.title: New Patient Call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller Derek Pereira, DOB 01/19/1982, interested in membership. Heard about us from a coworker. Currently has no doctor he sees regularly; last physical "a few years back" at his old primary care office. Employer PPO, card info entered. Membership agreement emailed. New patient appointment set for 11/7 at 8:30. Medical records release signed electronically, request faxed to prior office today.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
41-year-old man joining the practice. Feels well, no complaints today, mainly wants a doctor he can reach and a baseline checkup. Works as a sales manager for a corporate account team, a lot of driving and some air travel, sits a good part of the day.

PMH: none. No chronic illnesses, no hospitalizations.
PSH: tonsils out at age 7.
Meds: none, no supplements.
Allergies: none to medications.
Family: father with high blood pressure and type 2 diabetes. Mother with an underactive thyroid. Sister gets migraines.
Social: never used tobacco. Has 2-3 drinks on weekends, social. Single, lives in Westfield.
ROS: negative across systems; sleeps OK, mood good.

Exam: well appearing, vitals as recorded. HEENT unremarkable, TMs clear, oropharynx without lesions (tonsils surgically absent). Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement or nodes. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Extremities warm, no swelling. Neuro: cranial nerves grossly intact, face symmetric, strength and gait normal. Skin: nothing of note.

PHQ-2 0.

Assessment/plan:
1. Adult health maintenance. Baseline CBC, CMP, lipids. A1c given his father's diabetes. One-time hepatitis C and HIV screening, he agrees.
2. Immunizations: no record of a tetanus booster in at least 10 years per patient, Tdap today. Flu vaccine today.
3. Colon cancer screening starts at 45, will plan for it then.
4. Old records requested.

Follow up for a physical next fall, or message any time.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Derek, everything from Tuesday came back fine. Blood counts, kidney and liver numbers normal. Cholesterol is in a good range and your A1c shows no sign of diabetes. Hep C and HIV screens negative. Nothing to do here. Good to have a baseline on file.

documents.title: Records From Prior Primary Care Office
documents.author: MA
documents.body: 17 pages received by fax from the patient's previous primary care office, covering 2016 to 2021. Contents: three routine physical exams with normal findings, routine labs within normal ranges, influenza vaccines most years, COVID primary series documented. Surgical history lists remote tonsillectomy. No problem list entries, no medications. No tetanus booster documented in that span. Abstracted, original scanned under Media for PCP review.

documents.title: Employer Wellness Form
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hey, our company does a wellness credit on the insurance if a doctor signs off on a biometric form. Can I upload it here? It wants BP, height/weight and cholesterol from the last 12 months. Thanks.

documents.title: RE: Employer Wellness Form
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Yes, attach it to this thread. We'll fill it in from your November visit and labs and get it signed. It usually takes a couple of business days, we'll message when it's back.

documents.title: Form Completed
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Biometric screening form completed from 11/7/23 visit and labs, signed by PCP, uploaded back to patient via portal. Copy scanned.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly exam. Has been well since joining, no visits in between. Busy quarter at work, traveling twice a month. Walks on weekends, plays pickup basketball occasionally. Alcohol unchanged, weekends only. No tobacco.

No meds. NKDA.
ROS negative.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Comfortable. Ears, throat normal. No neck masses. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen benign. No peripheral swelling. Face symmetric, neuro nonfocal. Skin clear.

PHQ-2 negative.

A/P: healthy adult.
- CMP, lipids, A1c today (father's diabetes).
- Flu and COVID boosters given in clinic.
- Tdap current (11/2023).
- Colonoscopy or stool test discussion at 45.
See him next October.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Derek, your labs from the physical all look normal: sugar and A1c fine, kidneys and liver fine, cholesterol good. Same plan, recheck next year.

documents.title: RE: Lab Results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great, thanks doc.

documents.title: Triage Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pt called the after-hours line at 7:10. Woke up about an hour ago and the right side of his face feels heavy. Couldn't brush his teeth right, water ran out the corner of his mouth when he drank. He tried in the mirror and can't lift the right eyebrow either. Denies weakness or numbness in his arms or legs, no trouble getting words out, no double vision, no headache. Walking normally. Went to bed fine last night.

Whole right side including the forehead points toward a peripheral facial nerve problem rather than a stroke, but he needs to be examined today. ENT colleague has an 11:00 opening, booked it and sent the referral. Told him plainly: if any arm or leg weakness, slurred speech, vision change or the face gets worse on the way, go straight to the ED / call 911. He should not drive himself if anything changes. He understands, a friend is giving him a ride. Asked him to let me know what ENT says.

medications.sig: Take 3 tablets (60 mg) by mouth once daily with breakfast for 5 days, then 50 mg, 40 mg, 30 mg, 20 mg, 10 mg on days 6-10, then stop
Instill 1-2 drops in the right eye every 2-3 hours while awake

medications.drug_text: mineral oil 0.425 MG/MG / petrolatum 0.568 MG/MG Ophthalmic Ointment
medications.sig: Apply a small ribbon to the right eye at bedtime

documents.title: Otolaryngology Consultation
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OTOLARYNGOLOGY PRACTICE
Date of service: 06/24/2025
Re: Derek Pereira, DOB 01/19/1982
Allergies: NKDA

Thank you for the same-day referral. Mr. Pereira is a 43 year old man who noticed on waking today that the right side of his face felt heavy. He could not brush his teeth normally and lost water from his mouth when drinking. Food tastes bland to him. He denies any limb weakness. Otherwise healthy, no medications; tonsillectomy as a child. Never smoker, drinks socially on weekends.

Exam: right auricle, ear canal and drum normal. Left ear normal. Complete weakness of the right face, forehead included, upper and lower divisions. Limb strength and coordination normal.

Impression: acute right Bell palsy.

Plan: prednisone 60 mg daily x5 days then taper by 10 mg/day to off. Eye care discussed at length: lubricating drops through the day, ointment and taping the lid closed at night, sunglasses outdoors. Expect improvement over weeks. Return to me as needed, sooner for eye pain or redness, or no improvement by 3 months.

Otolaryngology

documents.title: Eye Question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw ENT last week, they said Bell's palsy and put me on the prednisone. Day 7 now. Question about the eye tape at night, it keeps coming off by morning. Is the ointment enough on its own? Eye feels a little dry when I wake up but not painful.

documents.title: RE: Eye Question
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Derek, thanks for the update, the doctor got the ENT letter. Keep using the ointment every night. For the tape, paper tape works better than the regular kind; close the lid gently first, then tape horizontally across the upper lid. Some people use a moisture shield/eye patch from the pharmacy instead. Mild dryness in the morning is common, use the drops right away. If the eye gets red, painful, or your vision blurs, call us the same day. Follow-up is on the books for 7/8.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two weeks after onset of right Bell palsy, seen by ENT the same day. Finished the prednisone taper on 7/3. Says the face is "coming back": he can tell the right side of his mouth is moving more, and the eyebrow twitches up a bit. Food is starting to taste like food again. Using drops several times a day and ointment at night, gave up on tape and bought a sleep shield. No eye pain, no redness, vision fine. Working from home mostly, video calls are the hardest part.

Exam: right face still weaker than left but improved per patient and compared with the ENT description. Slight brow elevation on the right. Right eye closes fully with effort, cornea looks clear, no injection. Mouth droops less at rest, smile asymmetric. Rest of cranial nerves normal. Ears normal.

A/P: right Bell palsy, recovering.
- Steroid course complete.
- Continue drops/ointment as needed until the eye closes easily on its own.
- Facial exercises in the mirror if he likes, no need for formal therapy right now.
- Reach out if recovery stalls or eye symptoms. Physical due in October, will reassess then.

documents.title: Update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick update since you asked me to keep you posted. Most people at work can't tell anymore. Smile is almost even, eye shuts on its own most of the time, only using the drops once or twice a day now. Just wanted to say thanks for getting me in so fast that morning.

documents.title: RE: Update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's really good to hear, it's moving in the right direction. Fine to taper the drops as you feel you need them. Keep the ointment at night until the eye is fully closing every time. See you at your physical in October.

medications.drug_text: mineral oil 0.425 MG/MG / petrolatum 0.568 MG/MG Ophthalmic Ointment

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, also closing the loop on the Bell palsy from June. He says his face has been back to normal for about a month. Eye closes completely, stopped the drops a few weeks ago and the ointment last week. Taste normal. No twitching or tearing with eating. Otherwise well. Still traveling for work. Weekend drinks unchanged, never smoker.

Meds: none current. NKDA.
ROS negative.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Face symmetric at rest and with brow raise, tight eye closure, smile and puffing cheeks; no synkinesis seen. Corneas clear. Ears and throat normal. Neck without nodes. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Neuro otherwise nonfocal. Skin unremarkable.

PHQ-2 0.

A/P:
1. Right Bell palsy, fully recovered. Removed from active problems. Drops and ointment off the list. Told him it rarely returns but to call right away if it does, since treatment works best early.
2. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c today. Flu and COVID vaccines given. Colorectal screening due after his 45th birthday in January 2027, we'll set it up then.
Next physical in a year.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Morning Derek. Labs from Friday are normal across the board: blood counts, chemistries, cholesterol and A1c. No changes needed.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
AREA HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT, brief visit summary
DOS 02/09/2026. Pt: Pereira, Derek, 44M. Allergies: NKDA. Meds: none.

CC: R face drooping x2 days.
HPI: Similar episode last June, seen by ENT then, recovered. Two days ago abrupt onset of R facial asymmetry. Food pockets between his teeth and R cheek, keeps biting inside of R lip, liquids dribble from R side of mouth. Denies head injury, rash, ear pain, recent cold symptoms.

Exam: R nasolabial fold flat, R oral commissure droops, R eye does not fully close with blink, R forehead does not wrinkle on brow raise. Facial sensation intact to LT and pinprick. Hearing grossly intact. Remaining CNs normal.

Dx: Bell's palsy, R, recurrent.
Dispo: home. Rx prednisone 60 mg daily x5d then taper over 5d. Artificial tears daytime, lubricating ointment qhs. F/u ENT and PCP this week. Return for new weakness elsewhere, vision change, eye pain.

documents.title: It came back
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Bad news, the Bell's palsy is back, same side. Started Saturday, I figured I was imagining it but by Monday it was obvious so I went to the ER last night. They said same thing as last time and gave me prednisone again plus the eye drops and ointment. I still had some of the old ointment. They told me to see ENT and you. Is this normal for it to come back??

documents.title: RE: It came back
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry Derek, that's frustrating. It does come back in a small number of people, sometimes on the same side. Take the full prednisone course as written, with food in the morning. Be strict about the eye: drops through the day, ointment and the shield at night if the lid isn't closing all the way. Please call the ENT office this week for a follow-up as the ER suggested. Anything new like weakness in an arm or leg, trouble speaking, eye pain or blurry vision, go back to the ED. Keep me posted on how it goes.

documents.title: Face update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Checking in like you asked. Face is almost back to normal again, maybe a little slower than last time. Eye closes fine now. Thanks.

documents.title: RE: Face update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad to hear it, thanks for letting me know. Reach out if anything changes.
